This method requires every financial transaction to be recorded with equal and opposite debits and credits. The Farolfi firm's ledger of 1299–1300 provides evidence of full double-entry bookkeeping.

bodies.thread:
In early modern Europe, double-entry bookkeeping carried theological connotations of the scales of justice and the symmetry of God's world.

This method requires every financial transaction to be recorded with equal and opposite debits and credits.

Every transaction is entered into at least two nominal ledger accounts to maintain accuracy and detect errors or fraud.

A debit entry represents a transfer of value to an account, while a credit entry represents a transfer from an account.

The earliest extant European accounting records following this system come from Amatino Manucci in the late 13th century.

Luca Pacioli first codified the system in his 1494 mathematics textbook, leading many to call him the father of accounting.

Double-entry accounting is the foundational system required to produce financial statements that comply with US GAAP and SEC reporting mandates for public companies.
